Hover near a boundary point or thrust line to preview its partner. Click or tap to lock it; leaving the plot restores the locked case. At overlapping lines, use the boundary selector to distinguish loads.

The thin construction follows resultant-force directions and turns on each block's vertical CoG line. Its blue concurrency points may lie outside the masonry; physical contact is checked at the joint-pressure diamonds.

Intrados opens (blue ×) Extrados opens (orange ×) Retained pivot ○ ◆ Joint pressure point Rigid-motion preview

The green shape illustrates onset kinematics. Relative rotations are capped at 10° and reduced if needed to avoid interpenetration. Gray blocks show the original geometry. The amplitude is not elapsed time or a predicted crack width; forces are checked in the original geometry.

Opening coverage across all boundary cases

Filled cells have an opening witness under at least one load; hollow cells are pressure-limit candidates without a verified opening witness. Different cells do not necessarily open together.

Selected-load joint diagnostics

Joint j lies between blocks j and j+1. t=0 is intrados; t=1 is extrados. Gap rates are normalized initial velocities. Zero end force does not imply positive separation.

Model, supports and sources

Block 0 is fixed. The right holder permits translation, prevents rotation, and can supply a moment. Both geometries use mesh-volume weights and friction coefficient 0.7 under vertical gravity.

This example analyzes opening of existing dry joints between rigid blocks. It does not model cracking within stones, elastic crack initiation, material crushing, or dynamic collapse. Cases without an opening-only witness retain their contact diagnostics. Unloaded but stationary endpoints remain closed in the selected mode.
